animatronics.name: PumpkinHead
animatronics._sinkVolume: Set 2026-09-06. PumpkinHead's speaker hangs off the ReSpeaker XVF3800, whose hardware attenuator saturates at wpctl 1.00 (see Renfield's note), so 1.00 is full hardware scale with zero digital gain and the correct clean canon. He had NO canon before this, which meant applyCanonicalSinkVolume had nothing to restore him to and a fleet master-volume fan-out could not be undone on this node. He was found at 0.40 (about -23 dB) with the operator reporting no audio. Proven audible at 1.00 by ear-check witnessed on his own camera mic (a 440 Hz tone rose from a ~25 noise floor to ~1800 during playback, and a TTS say showed speech-band peak/avg 5.99 vs 2.12 for silence). Room level is NOT yet operator-verified; if 1.00 is too quiet, raise the powered speaker's own knob rather than this number, which cannot go higher without pure software gain that clips.

animatronics.name: Renfield
animatronics._sinkVolume: CAPPED AT 0.70 on 2026-09-26 — USB POWER, not loudness. With the shake motor, eye rings and pen wired, every motion wake at 1.00 tripped the Pi 5's shared USB over-current sense (10 trips/min at 1.00, 2 at 0.85, 0 at 0.70/0.50, 0 with the sink muted while mic + session ran), and each trip re-enumerated the XVF3800 mid-sentence ('the ReSpeaker keeps rebooting'). The array's amp at full scale is the load; 0.70 is -9 dB on its hardware attenuator and the highest level measured clean. Set the room level on the powered speakers' own knob. Lift this back toward 1.00 only after the ReSpeaker moves to a POWERED USB HUB (then re-measure with `dmesg | grep -c over-current` across a wake). Previous note kept for the ear-check record: EAR-VERIFIED 2026-09-20 by the operator — a ~6 s TTS line at 1.00 was confirmed clear and loud enough in the room, which closes the fleet's last unheard volume. The measurement notes below stand and are why 1.00 is the ceiling worth using. Renfield's speakers hang off the ReSpeaker XVF3800 (a Pi 5 has no analog jack, so there is no other non-HDMI output), and that array's hardware attenuator SATURATES at wpctl 1.00: measured on the node 0.40=-23.00dB, 0.55=-15.00dB, 0.70=-9.00dB, 0.85=-4.00dB, 1.00=0.00dB, 1.30=0.00dB. So 1.00 is full hardware scale with zero digital gain, and anything above it (Orlok's 1.3) is pure PipeWire software gain that can clip. 1.00 is therefore the correct clean starting canon for a node whose amp is unknown — set the room level on the powered speakers' own knob first, and only move this number if that is not enough. It CANNOT be self-verified on this node: the XVF3800's USB descriptors declare both terminals 0x0405 Echo-canceling speakerphone, and a 0.40/0.70/1.00/1.40 playback sweep moved his own array's reading by 0.0 dB while the residual floor DROPPED 4 dB (AES gating), so his ears are structurally deaf to his own mouth. Needs a human in the room or an off-board mic.
animatronics._ip: 2026-09-27: his Pi 5 (192.168.8.224) fried and was replaced by a Raspberry Pi 4B that joined at 192.168.8.249. Before that: his Pi joined 2026-08-30 and held .224; this was null earlier, which made every CONFIG-driven path (npm run deploy:all included) skip him silently while reporting success. mDNS still overlays the live address at runtime (nodeDiscoveryService.overlay replaces ip and keeps config as the fallback), so this only has to be right enough to bootstrap SSH and keep him in the roster. animatronics.name: Alpha

It runs MonsterBox in Docker as a node with a part-less character (HAL eye picture) so the Orchestration Console has a home that drives no hardware. deploy:'console' (2026-10-16): npm run deploy:all rsyncs the SAME file set the animatronics get into ~/monsterbox-console/tree and rebuilds the container from it (scripts/deploy-console-node.sh), never over the git working tree; Alpha's code must never deviate from the fleet's. hardware:'none' keeps it out of fleet steps aimed at 'all'.
